module_intro: Subtopics: Narrative-Conditioned Bearish Delivery Sequences, Variations, Eligibility Conditions, Invalidation & Model Selection.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Modules 1--11. This module is the exact mirror of Module 11. Labels A--D remain pedagogical organising devices, not official ICT model names. Every short is an expression of the multi-timeframe narrative and bearish bias, never a standalone pattern.
module_objectives: State the core bearish delivery sequence that underlies most ICT short examples.
Distinguish the common bearish variations (FVG/OTE-centred, Breaker-centred, IFVG-centred, pure PD-array reaction) by the element that supplies the entry.
Apply the full eligibility checklist before any short entry.
Select the variation that best matches the active bearish narrative.
Define trade-level and narrative-level invalidation for every short.
Maintain full symmetry with the buy-side framework so that directional bias, not preference, decides whether a long or short model is used.

Every element is the mirror of the bullish skeleton. The advanced student who has internalised Module 11 needs only to invert direction, liquidity side, and premium/discount location.

concepts.name: Eligibility Checklist (All Bearish Variations)
concepts.definition:
Before any short variation is traded, confirm:

- Higher-timeframe (at least daily) bias is bearish and not invalidated.

- Named sell-side Draw on Liquidity is still active.

- Price is in premium of the controlling dealing range (or has just raided BSL and is returning into premium).

- Buy-side liquidity has been (or is being) raided as the origin of the leg.

- Bearish displacement and MSS are present.

- The entry array sits in the correct (premium) half of the range and is unmitigated (or is a valid bearish Breaker/IFVG).

- The expected kill zone supports the phase (manipulation complete, distribution active).

- Trade-level and narrative-level invalidation are defined before entry.

If any item fails, the variation is not eligible.

concepts.name: Invalidation Hierarchy
concepts.definition:
Every short carries two invalidation levels:

1371. Trade invalidation - close beyond the entry array's protective extreme or the displacement origin; ends the specific entry.

1372. Narrative / bias invalidation - the level or condition in the bearish bias statement; retires the bearish hypothesis and forbids further short models until a new bias is constructed.

Trade stop-out ≠ automatic narrative failure. Narrative failure does automatically retire open bearish assumptions.

concepts.name: Symmetry Discipline
concepts.definition:
The advanced student maintains strict symmetry:

1373. Long models require discount + SSL origin + bullish bias.

1374. Short models require premium + BSL origin + bearish bias.

1375. The same eligibility standards, invalidation hierarchy and narrative subordination apply to both sides.

Any tendency to favour one direction, or to relax standards on one side, is a process failure, not a market feature.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Example - Variation A (Bearish) in Context
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
Weekly bias: bearish toward 1.0500; premium; distribution phase. Daily bias (conditional): bearish after London BSL sweep + displacement + MSS.

London: Asian high and relative equal highs swept; bearish displacement; daily and 15-minute MSS; FVG at 1.0780 - 1.0810 (premium). OTE of the displacement leg overlaps the FVG.

Entry: retracement into FVG/CE during London or early New York. Stop above displacement origin. Targets: daily intermediate sell-side, then 1.0500.

This is the bearish mirror of Module 11's worked example, fully nested inside the multi-timeframe narrative and bias.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
The core bearish sequence is the consistent mirror of the bullish sequences in primary ICT teaching. FVG, Order Block, OTE, Breaker and IFVG as short-entry arrays are primary. Pedagogical variation labels and the eligibility checklist are advanced synthesis for symmetric, narrative-driven application.

***Source / Research note:** Primary orientation: ICT chart examples and mentorship demonstrating short entries after buy-side liquidity raids, displacement, structure shifts and premium PD-array retracements. Framework is the exact counterpart of Module 11.*

rules.statement: Eligibility checklist (all bearish variations) mirrors the bullish checklist: HTF (at least daily) bias bearish and not invalidated; named sell-side DOL still active; price in premium of the controlling range (or has just raided BSL and is returning into premium); buy-side liquidity has been (or is being) raided as the origin of the leg; bearish displacement and MSS present; entry array sits in the correct half of the range and is unmitigated (or is a valid Breaker/IFVG); expected kill zone supports the phase; trade-level and narrative-level invalidation defined before entry.

Symmetry discipline: long models require discount + SSL origin + bullish bias; short models require premium + BSL origin + bearish bias. The same eligibility standards, invalidation hierarchy and narrative subordination apply to both sides. Any tendency to favour one direction, or to relax standards on one side, is a process failure, not a market feature.

Every short carries two invalidation levels (mirroring the Buy Model): Trade invalidation -- close beyond the entry array's protective extreme or the displacement origin, ends the specific entry only. Narrative/bias invalidation -- the level or condition defined in the bias statement, retires the bearish hypothesis and forbids further short models until a new bias is constructed.

relationships.statement: This module is the exact mirror of Advanced Module 11 (ICT Buy Model): every variation, eligibility rule, and invalidation hierarchy applies symmetrically with direction reversed.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Do not short a premium FVG without HTF bearish bias. Do not treat variation labels as official ICT model names. Do not enter before the BSL raid and displacement. Do not use an undemonstrated IFVG or low-quality Breaker. Do not ignore narrative invalidation after repeated trade-level stops. Do not apply looser standards to shorts than to longs (or vice versa).

key_terms: Core bearish delivery sequence - HTF bias + BSL + displacement + MSS + premium array + sell-side DOL.
Variation A (bearish) - FVG / CE / OTE-centred continuation short.
Variation B (bearish) - Bearish Breaker continuation short.
Variation D (bearish) - HTF PD-array reaction refined by LTF confirmation.
Symmetry discipline - identical standards applied to both long and short models.
